SvmOrderIdentity.description: Identity of an order that settles through a Solana marketplace program. Such an order has no Seaport order hash, so `order_hash` is absent from its payload and it is addressed instead by `id`, the transaction signature that created it joined to the onchain state account holding it. Pass that `id` wherever an endpoint takes an order hash.

id.description: `creation_signature:order_state`. This is what an endpoint expecting an order hash takes for a Solana order, for example `GET /api/v2/orders/chain/solana/protocol/{protocol_address}/{order_hash}`. Base58 and case-sensitive; do not lowercase it.

order_state.description: Address of the onchain account holding the order's state. The second half of `id`.

creation_signature.description: Signature of the transaction that created the order. The first half of `id`.

asset_id.description: Mint of the asset the order is for, where the program records one. Absent otherwise.

SvmInstructionResponse.description: A Solana instruction to include in the transaction

program_id.description: Base58-encoded program address the instruction invokes

accounts.description: Accounts the instruction reads or writes, in order

SvmInstructionAccountResponse.description: An account referenced by a Solana instruction

signer.description: Whether the account must sign the transaction

writable.description: Whether the instruction writes to the account

SvmTransactionDetailsResponse.description: Everything needed to compile and sign a Solana v0 transaction. The client supplies a recent blockhash.

from.description: Base58-encoded address the transaction is built for

address_lookup_tables.description: Base58-encoded address lookup tables the compiled message must reference to stay under the transaction size limit

transaction_config.description: Present only when the transaction may be compiled as a v1 message. A v1 compiler drops the ComputeBudget instructions from `instructions` and places these values in the message header; legacy/v0 compilers ignore this field

SvmTransactionConfigResponse.description: Compute budget a v1 Solana message carries inline instead of as instructions

priority_fee_lamports.description: Total priority fee in lamports, as a decimal string

loaded_accounts_data_size_limit.description: Loaded accounts data size limit in bytes

heap_size_bytes.description: Requested heap frame size in bytes

FulfillmentActionsResponse.description: Response containing blockchain actions to execute to fulfill an order

steps.description: Ordered list of blockchain actions to execute. May include approval actions (e.g. setApprovalForAll) and a createListingsAction containing the Seaport order to sign. Serialized using proto3 JSON format — fields with default values (empty string, 0, false) may be omitted.

units_to_fill.description: Optional quantity of units to fulfill; defaults to remaining units for listings

include_optional_creator_fees.description: Whether to include optional creator fees in the fulfillment. If creator fees are already required, this is a no-op. Defaults to false.

order_hash.description: Seaport order hash, a 0x-prefixed 32-byte value. Absent on an order that settles through a Solana marketplace program, which has no Seaport identity and carries `svm_order` instead. Every EVM order has one.

protocol.description: Marketplace protocol a Solana order settles through, which is what tells you which identity shape the order uses. Absent on a Seaport order, whose payload is unchanged. Only orders we can build fulfillment for carry a value here.

svm_order.description: Identity of a Solana order, present in place of `order_hash`. A client that assumes `order_hash` is always set should read this field first and fall back to `order_hash`.

post.description: Returns the blockchain actions needed to fulfill a listing, for listings that cannot be fulfilled with Seaport calldata. A Solana listing is always fulfilled this way, because it settles through an onchain program rather than a signed order. The listing is addressed by the same identifier the get-order endpoint uses.

400.description: The request is invalid. Possible reasons: order not found, order not valid, order is not a listing, or no actions could be composed.
